The role sits within the Department of Neurology and involves acquisition and analysis of advanced structural MR imaging data at 3 and 7 tesla in patients with multiple sclerosis and other autoimmune diseases affecting the central nervous system. The focus is on lesions in the cerebral cortex, with the goal of understanding how lesion formation and repair differ in the cortex vs white matter and how these processes relate to brain atrophy, clinical course, and meningeal inflammation (evaluated using single cell transcriptomics of the cerebrospinal fluid).
cond_0105.responsibilities: Research projects may also include development and validation of new MRI techniques, working closely and regularly with researchers in the [Company name masked] Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Institute. You will stay in active contact with collaborators throughout the project, contributing to discussions and communicating findings as work progresses.
cond_0105.requirements: Candidates with MD, MD/PhD, or PhD are welcome to apply. Experience in MR image processing/analysis and basic computer programming skills are preferred.

The work focuses on lesions in the cerebral cortex, with the goal of understanding how lesion formation and repair differ in the cortex vs white matter and how these processes relate to brain atrophy, clinical course, and meningeal inflammation (evaluated using single cell transcriptomics of the cerebrospinal fluid). You will regularly connect with colleagues across the department and stay in close contact with the broader research team throughout the project.
cond_0366.responsibilities: Research projects may also include development and validation of new MRI techniques in active collaboration with researchers in the [Company name masked] Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Institute. You will communicate regularly with collaborators to clarify project goals and contribute to ongoing discussions about methods and findings.

MD, MD/PhD, or PhD

Basic computer programming skills

The focus is on lesions in the cerebral cortex, with the goal of understanding how lesion formation and repair differ in the cortex vs white matter and how these processes relate to brain atrophy, clinical course, and meningeal inflammation (evaluated using single cell transcriptomics of the cerebrospinal fluid).

cond_0503.requirements: Candidates with MD, MD/PhD, or PhD are welcome to apply. Experience in MR image processing/analysis and basic computer programing skills are preferred.

The focus is on lesions in the cerebral cortex, with the goal of understanding how lesion formation and repair differ in the cortex vs white matter and how these processes relate to brain atrophy, clinical course, and meningeal inflammation (evaluated using single cell transcriptomics of the cerebrospinal fluid).
